Orthokeratology (OrthoK) lenses are specially designed contact lenses worn overnight. They gently reshape the cornea while sleeping, allowing clear vision during the day without glasses or contact lenses.
We find that families find this particularly useful when their children are playing sports. There are families that prefer their kids to not wear glasses and they find this useful too.
In children, OrthoK lenses are also used as part of myopia management to help slow progression in selected cases. Proper evaluation, precise fitting, and regular follow-up are essential to ensure safety and effectiveness.

Doctors recommend OrthoK after assessing eye measurements, corneal health, and suitability for the child’s age and lifestyle.

Book an appointment to evaluate OrthoK suitability.

Myopia (short-sightedness) often begins in childhood and may increase as a child grows. Lately, we have been seeing this growth continue upto even 18-19 years of age which is a concern. The Myopia Control Clinic at Eye Solutions focuses on early assessment, monitoring progression, and offering evidence-based strategies to help manage myopia.

Each child undergoes a detailed vision and eye health evaluation, followed by personalised guidance based on age, eye measurements, and lifestyle factors. Management plans are designed to support long-term visual health while fitting into a child’s daily routine.

Early evaluation allows parents to understand progression patterns and available options clearly.

Book an appointment at the Myopia Control Clinic.

Squint occurs when the eyes do not align properly, causing each eye to focus in a different direction. In children, this can interfere with normal visual development and may lead to reduced vision in one eye if not monitored early. Some children may not complain of vision problems, making regular eye checks important.

In adults, squint can cause eye strain, headaches, double vision, or difficulty with depth perception. It may develop gradually or appear suddenly due to changes in vision, nerve function, or muscle balance.

Squint is not always constant and may appear only during fatigue, illness, or prolonged screen use. Early assessment helps identify whether the squint is intermittent or persistent and whether it affects visual function.

An eye examination allows doctors to evaluate eye alignment, vision, and binocular function and advise on observation, correction, or treatment when needed.

Book an eye check-up for squint assessment.

Squint (misalignment of the eyes) can affect vision, depth perception, and eye comfort in both children and adults. At Eye Solutions, squint management begins with a detailed evaluation to understand the type, cause, and impact on vision.

Treatment may involve glasses, exercises, or surgical correction, depending on individual findings. Squint surgery aims to improve eye alignment and visual coordination through a planned and measured approach.

Early evaluation helps determine the most appropriate course of care and timing of treatment.

Book an appointment for a squint evaluation.

Cataracts develop slowly and often go unnoticed in the early stages. Many people assume their changing vision is simply a part of ageing, but recognising early signs can help with timely evaluation and planning.

Common early symptoms include blurred or hazy vision, increased glare from lights, difficulty driving at night, faded colours, and frequent changes in spectacle power. Some people also notice that reading becomes harder even with updated glasses.

Cataracts are not an emergency condition, but regular eye check-ups are important to monitor progression. Early assessment allows your doctor to explain the condition, discuss lifestyle impact, and advise on the right time for treatment - if and when needed.

If you are experiencing persistent visual changes or feel your vision is not as sharp as before, an eye examination can help clarify the cause and guide you appropriately.

Book an eye check-up to understand your vision better

A comprehensive eye examination checks more than just vision. It includes vision and eye power assessment, cataract evaluation, eye pressure measurement, and screening for diabetic eye disease.

Using a wide-angle fundus camera, we can capture nearly 90% of the retina in a single image - often without dilating eye drops. This avoids the waiting time and temporary blurred vision that dilation can cause.

Eye pressure checks help detect changes that, if uncontrolled, may lead to a condition called glaucoma. These tests help doctors assess overall eye health and guide further care when needed.

Book an appointment for a comprehensive eye check-up.

Cataracts cause gradual clouding of the natural lens, leading to blurred vision, glare, and difficulty with daily activities. At Eye Solutions, cataract surgery is planned carefully after a detailed evaluation of your eye health and visual needs.

The procedure involves replacing the cloudy lens with a clear artificial lens to improve vision clarity. Our focus is on safe techniques, precise measurements, and a calm, patient-centric approach - from consultation to recovery.

If you or a family member are experiencing vision changes, an eye examination can help determine the next step.

Call now to schedule an evaluation.

I am sharing this review anonymously and intentionally not disclosing specific details of my case, as other members of my family are currently receiving treatment at this clinic. My intention is not to create conflict but to share my experience so that other patients can make informed decisions.
The doctor may be a skilled surgeon, but I would strongly recommend seeking a second opinion before proceeding with LASIK or any major treatment. In my case, LASIK was presented as the only option, but after further consultation elsewhere, I learned that it may not have been necessary.
I was also concerned that my records did not clearly document my eye power, a written treatment plan, or detailed examination findings. I was prescribed glasses that felt significantly stronger than what my eyes could comfortably tolerate, which resulted in considerable eye strain and discomfort. When I reported these issues, I was again advised that LASIK was the only solution.
This is only my personal experience, and others may have had different outcomes. However, I believe it is important for patients to ask questions, request proper documentation of their diagnosis and treatment plan, and seek a second opinion before making important decisions regarding their eye health.
I hope this feedback is taken constructively and helps both future patients and the clinic improve communication and patient care.
